apify.caption: How to start a new job with confidence and purpose! #xyz #fyp #foryoupage #newjob #sf #techtechtok
apify.subtitle_text: I just started my new job at a 500% company after selling my startup to them last week. And here's what I'm doing to get started and how I'm hitting the ground running. First week of any new job should be really focused on laying the ground work in the foundation across three different areas. Vision, the relationships and the systems. Monday, one of the first things that I did was I had a one on one with the CTO and the co founder and really tried to understand what the vision is for the company as a whole, but also for the engineering team. Where does he see us going over the next year? What are the gaps, where are the opportunities and how do we fit in as a team given that we were just acquired? And you wanna remember that people at different levels have different perspectives and you wanna ask the right questions based on their level of perspective. So you're not gonna ask the CEO or the co founder about how to log into snowflake. You're gonna ask them about the strategic vision of the company for the next year. Set a good idea of the vision of the company, of the engineering department as well as our team. I started to work on the relationships. I went into our HR platform which is rippling and I looked at the org chart and tried to understand how many teams are there. How is the organization? Structured, who are the team leads? Who reports to who? What are the teams that I'm gonna be interacting with? I then reach out to those team leads on Slack instead of one on ones with them to understand who are they as people, what do they care about, what are their problems, what are the things that they're working on? And then also introduce myself. And last, I started to think about systems, some part of the engineering organization. I want to get a good idea of the different tools and systems that people are using. What is the STLC look like? What are the workflows look like? And I'm just trying to understand the status quo. After that, I really want to understand how data moves through the organization, mainly because I'm gonna be responsible for a lot of this data, but also because a lot of teams are generally structured around different data flows. So I really wanna understand who are the producers of data, where are the consumers, and what does the general integration path look like? You can do this in any industry, in any company, in any role. But it's also important to understand the expectation of your role, of your level, and of the company you're coming into. For example, if you're joining a really early stage startup as an engineer, you're probably gonna wanna ship code like day one or day two. Versus I'm coming in at a staff level of a 500% company. They're not going to want me to write a product requirement DOC right away because I don't have enough context of the business, of the vision, of the strategy of the different teams. They really want me to understand that first, work with our engineering team and figure out what is the right solution moving forward. And that takes time. And that's why I spend a lot of my time early on building those relationships, understanding the systems and the data flows, understanding the vision, before I get to doing, like, very tactical day to day work. As they say, you only get one chance to make a good first impression. I think taking advantage of that first week so you can show people that you're serious and that you're somebody who can be trusted and is gonna work hard is gonna make all the difference down the line.

apify.caption: Replying to @𝓪𝓲𝓮𝓪 Best Lateral Raise - Cable VS Dumbbell 🤔
apify.subtitle_text: should you do cable lateral raises or dumbbell lateral raises well there was actually a recent study done comparing the two lateral raise variants on 24 resistance-trained men and women and after an eight week intervention compromising two weekly workouts of five sets of lateral raises to failure with shoulder AB and ADduction range of motion standardized and matched between conditions muscle thickness of the proximal and distal regions of the lateral or rather side delt was assessed what researchers found was that there were no significant differences between conditions or rather exercises, again, in terms of muscle growth growth however, when looking at the results a little deeper the cable lateral raise resulted in slightly more distal region hypertrophy while the dumbbell lateral raise resulted in slightly more proximal region growth that being said, although it’s clear there is different regional hypertrophy present with both exercises the curve is more narrow for distal growth with the cable lateral raise versus the curve for proximal growth with the dumbbell lateral raise meaning that there were smaller deviations between measurements in the sample for the former condition and as a result suggesting that there was more regional hypertrophy happening in the distal region with the cable variant than there was in the proximal region with the dumbbell variant this is likely due to leverages of subdivisions within the lateral delt and the addition of stretch-mediated hypertrophy adaptations resulting in slightly more growth for the distal region as the subjects perform the cable lateral raise with a lengthened biased profile by having the pulley set to above knee height so it was hardest at the bottom in the stretch remember that trained lifters still need to maintain those stretch adaptations or obtain them in the first place from doing the exercise loaded in the lengthened position and if they don't or have yet to they are then subject to more growth when exposed to it whereas with the dumbbell variant you're loading the mid range since gravity acts down so it was hardest for subjects when the arm was parallel with the ground in other words, it was hardest in a different part of the range of motion as for what this tells us and what my recommendations are all lateral raise variants will produce very similar muscle gains since the lateral delt has great leverage through its entire joint range of motion but they do stimulate slightly more or less hypertrophy in different regions of the lateral delt which is known as regional hypertrophy based on the resistance profile in other words based on where the most effort is required in the lift the lateral delt also happens to be on the descending limb of the length-tension relationship a bit so they are susceptible to stretch-mediated hypertrophy to a small degree consequently if you're a beginner lifter specifically my recommendation would be to do a unilateral cable lateral raise that loads the lengthened position or rather the bottom part of the movement more often or frequently as it may be better for muscle gains since you likely won't have stretch-mediated hypertrophy adaptations fully maxed out yet otherwise my recommendation is to just do a mix of lateral raise variants over the course of a macrocycle or calendar year to ensure that we are maximizing overall growth though with stable variants being done more often as stability is our friend when it comes to muscle hypertrophy I would also include a lengthened biased lateral raise at least every other training block to help maintain stretch adaptations as well with that being said I do wish this study went on for longer though perhaps on untrained lifters as well to see if stretch-mediated hypertrophy adaptations as well as leverages would have caused a greater difference between conditions as despite the lateral delts having good leverage throughout its whole joint range of motion its best relative leverage is in the lengthened position at around 40 degrees of abduction mind you I don't think 8 weeks is very long for trained lifters so I hope this research apify.subtitle_text: I recently had the best chicken over rice in Miami at d C G. And now I'm craving it again. So let's make it at home. I also seared the chicken in some ghee until it was golden on both sides. Take that out of the pan and then chop it up into these rough cubes. Then add it back to the pan on a high heat for a couple more minutes with a little more tandoori spice for added colour and flavour. You have to serve this with a little lettuce, tomato, cucumber salad on the side. Drench it in some white sauce, add some hot sauce, fresh parsley and enjoy.

apify.subtitle_text: The four low back standards before getting back to sports or lifting. One. Back extension ISO hold 2 minutes pain free 2. Back extension full range reps going for 30 controlled and inverted reps. 3. Outer hip drop set being able to hold 30 seconds at each position without any spasm, pain, or flare up at the low back. This one is for the hips, but directly affects the low back. 4. Pain free side bending, slowly building body weight standing reps, then weighted standing reps, then body weight reps off the back extension machine. These four steps are the foundation to further low back training.

The creator narrates the instructions while performing or overseeing the exercises in various gym environments, emphasizing these steps as a foundational approach to low back training and injury prevention.
